summary_html: **Healthcare encounters** that reveal suspected abuse or neglect trigger reporting obligations. Federal law governs mandatory reporting in federal facilities and coordination with state systems.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — state reporter systems and protections  
- **Victims of Child Abuse Act (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — mandates in federal settings, CAC coordination

key_cases.holding: Reversing partial summary judgment as to one reporter and affirming as to another, the court held that immunity for reporting suspected child abuse under I.C. § 16-1606 is decided by the court rather than a jury but must be resolved under the traditional summary-judgment standard, and that a genuine fact issue existed on whether one reporter acted in bad faith.
key_cases.relevance: The reporter's hospital presentation of the child was part of the reporting course of conduct assessed for good faith.
key_cases.quote: the traditional summary judgment standard applies in the context of liability of persons reporting instances of suspected child abuse

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: Reversing summary judgment for the officers and the city, the court held that children may be seized from parents without prior judicial authorization only on reasonable cause to believe the child faces imminent danger of serious bodily injury, that reasonable cause is a jury question, and that subjecting seized children to invasive medical examinations without judicial authorization or parental notification implicates the family's right to make medical decisions.
key_cases.relevance: Invasive investigatory medical examinations of a seized child require judicial authorization and parental notification.
key_cases.quote: The right to family association includes the right of parents to make important medical decisions for their children

search_keywords: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare

state_agency.name: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare, Child and Family Services

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — Idaho Code § 16-1605(1)
Physicians, hospital residents, interns, nurses, coroners (named in Idaho Code § 16-1605(1))
School teachers, day care personnel, social workers (named in Idaho Code § 16-1605(1))
Hospital or similar institution staff report through the person in charge of the institution, who makes the necessary reports — Idaho Code § 16-1605(1)
Only exception: a duly ordained minister of religion, as to a confession or confidential communication received in his ecclesiastical capacity — Idaho Code § 16-1605(3)
reporting_details: Idaho is a universal mandatory reporting state: any person who has reason to believe a child under 18 has been abused, abandoned, or neglected must report it to law enforcement or the Department of Health and Welfare within 24 hours, failure to report is a misdemeanor, and the only exception is a duly ordained minister of religion as to a confession made in his ecclesiastical capacity (Idaho Code § 16-1605(1), (3), (4)).

other: Placing child for care or adoption in violation of law

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately (Priority I); child seen within 48 hours (Priority II); worker responds within 3 calendar days and child seen within 5 calendar days (Priority III)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Any variance from the response priorities must be documented in the family's case file with the action taken and reviewed and signed by the Child and Family Services Supervisor (IDAPA 16.06.01.554)

notice_requirements.timing: In writing, at the time of or within seventy-two (72) hours after the department makes first contact directly and in person with the parents, guardians, or other persons having legal custody of the child (Idaho Code § 16-1649(2)); the notification must be on a form prescribed by the department (§ 16-1649(4))
content_required: The right to refuse to answer questions

The right to obtain an attorney at their own expense, consult with that attorney, and have that attorney present during an investigation (the department is not authorized to appoint or obtain an attorney)
The right to refuse entry to their home or other real property

The right to refuse the questioning of any minor children in their home or on their property, unless a court of competent jurisdiction has issued an order authorizing a particular entry, questioning, or examination
A statement that if the safety of the child cannot be determined, the department may request assistance from a law enforcement agency or seek a court order
notice_requirements.defective_notice_consequence: Failure by the department to provide the notification in a specific investigation shall not affect the department's ability to conduct that investigation or to carry out its duties under the Child Protective Act (Idaho Code § 16-1649(5))
